sections.html:
Clark County is Nevada's southernmost and most populous county. It had 2,265,461 residents in 2020, about 70% of the state's population, on 8,061 square miles of land. Five incorporated cities sit inside it, among them Las Vegas (the county seat), Henderson and North Las Vegas, along with 21 unincorporated towns.

That last detail trips up sellers. More than a million residents live in unincorporated areas yet use a Las Vegas mailing address. Whether your house sits inside a city or in an unincorporated town decides which planning, code and utility offices you deal with, although the county bills the property tax either way.

Three county offices split the work: the Assessor sets values, the Treasurer sends bills and collects, and the Recorder files deeds and takes transfer tax. The state Department of Taxation sets rates for each tax district.

  • Treasurer: 500 S Grand Central Pkwy, Box 551220, Las Vegas, NV 89155-1220
  • Treasurer phone: (702) 455-4323, open Monday through Thursday, 7:30 am to 5:30 pm, closed Friday through Sunday
  • Assessor appeals line: (702) 455-4997

A real property bill is mailed once per fiscal year. If yours has not shown up by August 1, request a copy through the automated phone system. Under NRS 361.480, a bill that never arrived is no excuse for paying late. Buyers who close mid-year and owners whose lender stopped paying should call the office to get a bill.

The full amount is due the third Monday in August. When the total tops $100 you may pay in installments instead, though these are not quarterly payments. The installment dates are the third Monday in August and the first Mondays of October, January and March, and you have 10 days after each due date before a penalty applies. The penalty grows as more installments go unpaid:

Installments latePenalty on each late installment
One4%
Two9% on the first, 5% on the second
Three15%, 11% and 6%
Four22%, 18%, 13% and 7%

With an escrow account, still confirm your mortgage company paid on time. The responsibility stays with you. The Treasurer's page offers payment reminders by email or text.

Anything still unpaid at the end of April is advertised as delinquent in the local newspaper and on the Treasurer's website. If the balance remains open at close of business on the first Monday in June, the Treasurer holds the property through a two-year redemption period.

To redeem, you pay the taxes, the accruing taxes, penalties and costs, plus 10% yearly interest counted from the original due date. For property found abandoned, the tax receiver can cut the process to one year under NRS 361.567. When nothing is paid, the property is deeded to the County Treasurer as trustee and can go to public auction.

Auctions generally happen at least once a year, often in spring. Registration is capped at 280 bidders and a $5,000 deposit applies. Property deeded to the trustee after three consecutive delinquent fiscal years, or two when abandoned, is eligible for auction.

A house already on a delinquent list can still be sold before redemption ends, and the payoff comes out of the closing. Current rules are on the county's real property tax page.

sections.h2: How is a home valued, and how do I appeal?
sections.html:
The Assessor uses the cost method. It starts with the replacement cost of the building, subtracts depreciation, and adds the market value of the land. Depreciation runs at 1.5% per year of effective age, capped at 50 years, and values are refreshed annually.

The tax rate depends on your tax district, so a neighbor in another district may pay a different amount. Homes that qualify for the 3% or 8% abatement owe the lower of the calculated tax or the capped amount.

  • Appeal forms are available from the Assessor in December.
  • The deadline is January 15, or the next business day when that date falls on a weekend or holiday.
  • If the County Board of Equalization sides with the Assessor, the next stops are the State Board and then District Court.

The Clark County Recorder charges $2.55 for each $500 of value, or fraction of it, based on the full price or estimated fair market value. The state's base is $1.95 per $500 in every county, and Clark County adds $0.60.

Some transfers are exempt under NRS 375.090. A Declaration of Value must be filed with the deed, and the Recorder supplies it free. The county's online calculator gives an estimate only, and your title company will prepare the exact amount at closing.

Taxes are settled at closing like any other lien. The title company requests a payoff from the Treasurer, pays it out of your proceeds and splits the current installment between you and the buyer. Owners who are behind should pull the parcel's status on the Treasurer's payment site first and sort out which installments are open.

Timing deserves attention. An installment may come due soon after you sign a contract, and the buyer and seller each owe a share of the year. If an escrow lender missed a payment, fix that before the closing date, because a surprise balance can hold up a sale.

sections.h2: What Clark County sellers run into
sections.html:
The size of the county creates most of the surprises.

  • Tax rates that vary by district, so a neighbor's bill is not a guide to yours.
  • An installment due soon after a sale is signed.
  • An escrow lender that missed a payment.
  • Inherited property with taxes unpaid across several installments.

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses as-is across the county and can close around a tax balance, with the payoff coming out of the sale. We do not promise a price before seeing the property. Look up your parcel on the Treasurer's payment site as a first step.

faqs.q: When are Clark County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The third Monday in August, with installments on the first Mondays of October, January and March if the total tops $100. Payment within 10 days of each date avoids a penalty.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost in Clark County?
faqs.a: One late installment adds 4%. With two late, the first draws 9% and the second 5%, and the figures climb again at three and four.

faqs.q: What is Clark County's transfer tax?
faqs.a: $2.55 per $500 of value: the state base of $1.95 plus $0.60 added in this county.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Clark County?
faqs.a: January 15, filed with the County Board of Equalization. Forms come out in December, and the Assessor's appeals line is (702) 455-4997.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clark County house that has delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale before redemption ends is allowed, and the taxes, penalties and interest come out of your proceeds at closing.
